page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, running on dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors with x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 4.5 GHz, supported by 768.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per vCPU core). It integrates 5,669 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage and includes vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, while lacking dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier computational and memory performance. The configuration scores in the top 10% across stress-ng single-core (3,775.48) and multi-core (176,827.47) benchmarks, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 118,358.18. Memory throughput reaches 9,789.61 GB/sec in small-block cached reads and 312.86 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations. It also achieves 143.37 million Redis SET operations per second and handles multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 590.13 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is centered around dense core scaling and bundled high-capacity NVMe storage. Combining 768.0 GB of RAM with local solid-state drives minimizes latency and reliance on external network volumes for ephemeral caching or scratch space. For CPU-based machine learning inference, it processes 5,688.73 tokens/sec on small models and 59.46 tokens/sec generation on 7B models, though the absence of discrete GPUs limits raw efficiency for massive deep learning workloads relative to dedicated accelerator platforms.

Microsoft Azure E96ads_v7 is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory relational and NoSQL databases, extensive caching layers, high-volume data analytics, large-scale ETL pipelines, and CPU-driven language model inference.

It provides 768.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core) and bundles 5,669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. The instance demonstrates top-tier benchmark results across compute, compression, and memory operations, recording 143.37 million Redis SET operations per second and 176,827.47 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Its high memory-to-core ratio and rapid NVMe scratch space deliver high resource density for data-intensive processing without external storage overheads. The server is suited for in-memory databases, real-time caching, enterprise analytics, and CPU-bound model inference.
